repairs.value: Strongest feature: Sechler candidly rejects the severe version of Christianity in which everyone lacking explicit belief in Jesus’s resurrection is condemned, a charitable concession that directly answers Clifton’s hiddenness analogy and justifies the exceptional calibration-and-charity score of 90. Principal limitation: The concession narrows what Christianity may plausibly claim but, as the evidence-warrant score of 65 and responsiveness score of 72 indicate, it offers no positive account of how the remaining theology treats sincere nonbelief or avoids Clifton’s maternal-relationship concern. Live burden: Sechler needs to explain which salvation conditions replace hard intellectual exclusivism and why those conditions make divine hiddenness compatible with the loving relationship Christianity attributes to God. Locked score: The overall 78 appropriately rewards his honest, precise retreat from universal condemnation while retaining a substantial penalty because rejecting an especially harsh doctrine does not establish the plausibility of the alternative he continues to defend.

Strongest feature: Clifton accepts Sechler’s evidential-chip framing and sharpens it with Opie’s theoretical-virtues comparison, proposing that Christianity and its competitor be assessed by explanatory reach relative to their commitments and costs, which supports the strong responsiveness score of 85 and calibration-and-charity score of 89. Principal limitation: The evidence-warrant score of 70 reflects that endorsing a comparative method does not yet identify the relevant costs, assign their relative importance, or demonstrate that Christianity explains less than its alternative. Live burden: Clifton must apply the proposed accounting to concrete features of divine hiddenness and hell, showing which worldview explains sincere nonbelief more economically and why any added assumptions count as genuine theoretical liabilities. Locked score: The overall 81 properly recognizes a clear and cooperative methodological advance while withholding a higher mark until the comparative framework produces an actual, defensible balance sheet rather than an agreed instruction to compare.
